questions.:question/problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x &=5 \\ -5x+6y &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First, let's write the system so that both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation. The variable $y$ does not appear in the first equation, but this just means its coefficient is $0.$ So, we get

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+0y &=5 \\ -5x+6y &=-8\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
A = {\left[ \begin{array}{cc}2 & 0 \\ - 5 & 6\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
\mathbf{b} = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}5 \\ - 8\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
\mathbf{x} = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

$$
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}2 & 0 \\ - 5 & 6\end{array} \right]}

{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}5 \\ - 8\end{array} \right]}.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-5y &=-3x \\ 6+x &=-2+y\end{aligned}\right.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}3x-5y &=0 \\ x-y &=-8.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ where

$$
A = {\left[ \begin{array}{cc}3 & - 5 \\ 1 & - 1\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
\mathbf{b} = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}0 \\ - 8\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
\mathbf{x} = {\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ becomes

$$
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}3 & - 5 \\ 1 & - 1\end{array} \right]}
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}0 \\ - 8\end{array} \right]}.
$$

questions.:question/problem:
What is the system of equations represented by
$$
{\left[ \begin{array}{cc}10 & - 15 \\ 1 & 0\end{array} \right]}
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}x \\ y\end{array} \right]}
=
{\left[ \begin{array}{c}5 \\ - 2\end{array} \right]}?
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The  $2\times 2$ matrix represents the coefficients of $x$ and $y,$ while the $2\times 1$ column vector on the right-hand side represents the constants of the equations. So, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}10x-15y &=5 \\ 1x+0y &=-2\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Simplifying both equations in the system, we get

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-3y &=1 \\ x &=-2.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=y-1 \\ x &=-y+1\end{aligned}\right.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and  both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=-1 \\ x+y &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$

$$
\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -10\end{bmatrix}.

questions.:question/problem:
What is the system of equations represented by

$$
\begin{bmatrix}8 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}16 \\ -18\end{bmatrix}?
$$

The corresponding system of equations is

| { | {{field-1}} | $=$ | $\,4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | $=$ | $\,\,3.$ |  |
questions.:question/worked-solution:
The $2\times 2$ matrix encodes the coefficients of $x$ and $y$, and the $2\times 1$ vector on the right gives the constants, so the system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}8x-4y &=16 \\ -6x+12y &=-18\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Dividing the first equation by $4$ and the second by $-6$ gives the simplified system

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-y &=4 \\ x-2y &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

which matches the entries shown above.

contents.:tutorial/content:
Matrices can be used to represent systems of equations, such as the following:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+3y &=5 \\ 4x\text{ }-\text{ }5y &=-1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

For a $2\times 2$ system like the one above, we put the coefficients of the system into a $2\times 2$ matrix, called the **coefficient matrix**:

$$
A = \begin{bmatrix}{\color{red}{2}} & {\color{red}{3}} \\ {\color{red}{4}} & {\color{red}{-5}}\end{bmatrix}
$$

Each row has the coefficients of one of the equations in the system, and each column consists of the coefficients of one particular variable.
We also have the $2\times 1$ column vectors

$$
\mathbf{b}=\begin{bmatrix}{\color{blue}{5}} \\ {\color{blue}{-1}}\end{bmatrix} \quad \text{and} \quad
\mathbf{x}=\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix},
$$

where $\mathbf{b}$ consists of each constant on the right side of the system and $\mathbf{x}$ contains the variables.
With these matrices, we can write our system as $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b},$ or

$$
\begin{bmatrix}{\color{red}{2}} & {\color{red}{3}} \\ {\color{red}{4}} & {\color{red}{-5}}\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}
=\begin{bmatrix}{\color{blue}{5}} \\ {\color{blue}{-1}}\end{bmatrix}.
$$

We can write any system of two equations with two variables in this form.
Just to check that the above equation is true, let's multiply out the left-hand side to see if it equals the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax & =\begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 \\ 4 & -5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}2x+3y \\ 4x\text{ }-\text{ }5y\end{bmatrix} \\  & =\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =b\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
